Neither admissible closing ground applies: wrong_sign_resolved requires the WHOLE week-blocked interval on the wrong side of zero and this one is [-0.6148, +0.3009]; positive_control_bound requires the instrument to have been PROVEN able to detect an effect of THIS size, and the control only proved detection of a +48.4-point leak; no_split_half_reliability is unavailable both because the correctly-specified across-season split-half reads Spearman-Brown 0.8271 (far above the 0.10 ceiling the ground admits) and because a deterministic calendar fact has zero measurement error. Per AGENTS.md an interval containing zero is the EXPECTED shape for a real small signal at this evaluator's ~2-point resolution, never grounds to close.
cfb_rest_home_off_bye_on_benchmark_era_2.description: CFB replication of NFL travel_rest_home_off_bye: home_rest >= 13 days (side-specific absolute threshold) added as ONE extra column to the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm, which already carries rest_diff. Paired candidate-minus-baseline forced-pick accuracy delta; positive = the extra column helped. NFL predicted direction on home_cover: positive. ERA SLICE 2021-2025 only.
cfb_rest_home_off_bye_on_benchmark_era_2.notes: ERA SLICE 2021-2025 of cfb_rest_home_off_bye_on_benchmark, recorded because this cell's two eras carry OPPOSITE SIGNS, so the pooled figure is an average across a sign flip and must not be read as either era's magnitude (owner rule 'era magnitude, not presence'). Sibling era slice: 2012-2019 +0.093 pts P+ 0.632. Pooled over both eras: -0.145 pts P+ 0.273. Season-blocked secondary for this era: 95% [-1.3133, +0.3296] P+ 0.0680. 430 flagged games in this era. NOT an independent vote against its own pooled entry or the other era slice -- same window, same games, decomposed. Close-graded CFB: the CFB line archive is opener plus an unidentified-time resolved quote and no source records quote observation times (docs/cfb_data.md), so CFB can be graded at a close proxy and NEVER at a verified opener; this settles no NFL play/no-play or promotion decision. THE BASELINE ALREADY CARRIES rest_diff: nfl_ats.cfb_features.CFB_MODEL_FEATURE_COLUMNS (35 columns) includes rest_diff, so this is a MARGINAL on top of a model that already prices the linear rest difference, not a test of whether rest matters. NFL sibling entry: travel_rest_home_off_bye. The four cells of this battery are CORRELATED SUBSETS OF ONE WINDOW (the same 8,933 scored games, overlapping flags by construction) and are NOT independent votes -- do not sign-test-pool them. OVERLAP DISCLOSURE: separate pooling family cfb_rest_bye_replication, NEVER pooled with cfb_bias_battery. registry entries cfb_bias_battery_bye_week_rest_edge (rest edge >=6d) and cfb_bias_battery_short_week_rest_disadvantage (rest edge <=-4d) are SUBSET COVER RATE VS COMPLEMENT measurements on an overlapping CFB population -- a different quantity from this harness's paired accuracy delta of the XLG-03 estimator with exactly one extra column; AGENTS.md's commensurability rule forbids pooling non-commensurable comparators. Reliability recorded is the ACROSS-SEASON odd/even-YEAR split-half of the team's own propensity (own_off_bye_13): Pearson r +0.7052, Spearman-Brown 0.8271, P+ 1.0000, n_team_units 135. The repo-standard WITHIN-season odd/even-WEEK instrument reads r -0.3368 on the same panel; that is a structural artifact of a compositionally constrained calendar quantity (a team-season holds a fixed number of days and games, so extra rest in one part is arithmetically less rest elsewhere), not evidence about the trait -- docs/cfb_rest_bye_replication.md section 5. Seed 20260901, 1,000 bootstrap draws. Within-week permutation null (200 draws, standalone run artifacts/cfb_rest_bye_replication/20260901T192914Z): mean +0.015 pts, sd 0.204, 95% [-0.414, +0.403] -- the harness manufactures no effect. Positive control (this column replaced by the realised ats_margin, artifacts/cfb_rest_bye_replication/20260901T193234Z): +48.405 pts, P+ 1.000, 95% [+47.374, +49.464] -- the full 36-column ridge fit detects a large effect, which bounds NOTHING at the sub-1-point scale in question. XLG-03 baseline forced-pick accuracy on this population: 51.595%.
